reason: Concordia's published honour roll for the A. Ross Seaman Leadership Development Fund names every bursary winner from 1989 to 2006 and describes each one's character, career and camp service in a paragraph. Twenty-seven of those citations mention Kanawana. The people are living private individuals, most of them students at the time, the youngest awarded within twenty years of this reading. The material is laudatory and the university published it, so nothing is being protected from disclosure; what is avoided is this wiki assembling a searchable biography of a private person out of an honour roll. The institutional finding -- that Kanawana was a standing feeder community for the fund across nearly two decades -- is written into wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md in full, without names. Two individual details are kept without names because their subjects are Seaman and a camp tradition: a Human Relations Award winner's testimony that she 'caught the leadership bug early in her professional career as a camp nurse, under the mentorship of Ross Seaman', and a Capitaine selection for the L&V games by a man at camp from the summer of 1992.
embargo_basis: living private individuals under CLAUDE.md Phase 2 section 7; not a personal assessment, so the 75/100-year default does not apply. This is a decision to summarise rather than to roster.
note: NOT AN EMBARGO BLOCK. Nothing is written into an article inside markers; the roster is simply not reproduced. This record exists so a later pass can tell the difference between a source that says nothing and an editor who decided not to write something down. The names are in the booklet at the Internet Archive identifier in the source record.

reason: A roster of thirteen named boys aged twelve to sixteen from Kanawana's 1973 Wilderness Camp, each graded into one of two award tiers the programme's director invented that summer. Everything in it is favourable -- all thirteen passed -- and the source document is public, digitized by Concordia and readable on the Internet Archive. It is labelled anyway because the two tiers are an assessment of named children who are probably living, one tier's criterion being 'an evident degree of comfortability in the woods'. The institutional content -- thirteen campers, the age range, that all succeeded, seven at Wilderness I and six at Wilderness II -- is carried unembargoed in f_5478 and written openly in the article. The two counsellors are named unembargoed, being staff rather than campers.
